chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Muhammad Abdullah al-Sarraj, raised it to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:
Patience is to Faith as the head is to the body, and there is no Faith for the one who has no patience.

key_terms.الصَّبْرُ: Patience, perseverance, or steadfastness in the face of adversity or divine command.
key_terms.الْإِيمَانُ: Faith, belief, or conviction in God and His commands.
key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: At the status of / in the position of.

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between patience and faith in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam Ali al-Rida (or Ali ibn al-Husayn depending on the chain interpretation) to establish patience as the structural integrity of faith, a concept central to Shia ethical theology. This metaphor underscores that while belief may exist in theory, it remains functionally incomplete without the steadfastness (sabr) required to navigate trials, reflecting the Shia emphasis on practical piety. The hadith thus serves as a foundational text for understanding how spiritual resilience validates one's religious commitment.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Muhammad Abdullah Al Sarraj, 
(It has been narrated) raising it to Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The patience from the Emān is at the status of the head to the body, and there is no Emān for the one who has no patience for him’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from abu Muhammad ‘Abd Allah al-Sarraj who has narrated in a marfu’ manner from Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) who has said the following: “Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) has said, ‘
Patience is to belief as the head is to the body. One who does not have patience has no belief.’”
